item.title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01949-x

Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.
item.dc:title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities

item.title: Making ammonia at the water’s edge
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01982-w

Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can make ammonia from nitrogen and water under mild conditions, but slow nitrogen delivery and product build-up limit output. Now, a floating solar interface couples nitrogen reduction with evaporation, greatly speeding up ammonia formation and concentrating a high-purity product in the condensate.
item.dc:title: Making ammonia at the water’s edge

item.title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01981-x

Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.
item.dc:title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
